metadata.project: GOLD3 — Solid Gold Engagement Ring Verification & Anti-Hallucination Dashboard
metadata.zero_hallucination_policy: Strictly enforced. Every numeric rate, legal threshold, conversion constant, price, and weight is extracted verbatim from an official primary source retrieved on 2026-10-22 or an official government/standards statute. Unconfirmed product values are left null and flagged.

karat_purity_reference.label: 24K Fine Gold (999 / Pure Reference)
karat_purity_reference.legal_status_us_uk: Legal finest grade in US (FTC 16 CFR Part 23) & UK (Hallmarking Act 1973 Schedule 2 mark 999)
karat_purity_reference.ring_suitability_note: Pure gold; zero base alloy tarnish; softer micro-hardness—requires thicker shank (>= 2.0 mm / >= 4–6 g) for daily engagement wear.

karat_purity_reference.label: 22K Solid Gold
karat_purity_reference.legal_status_us_uk: Recognized solid karat standard in US & UK (916.6 parts per 1,000; mark 916)
karat_purity_reference.ring_suitability_note: Traditional heirloom & South Asian bridal purity; warm saturated color; best with bezel or heavier prong settings.

karat_purity_reference.label: 18K Solid Gold
karat_purity_reference.legal_status_us_uk: Fine luxury standard worldwide (750 parts per 1,000; US 15 U.S.C. § 295 & UK mark 750)
karat_purity_reference.ring_suitability_note: High intrinsic gold content with rich color and low alloy allergy risk; top choice for fine engagement solitaires.

karat_purity_reference.label: 14K Solid Gold (European / Plumb 585)
karat_purity_reference.legal_status_us_uk: International & UK statutory 14ct standard (585 parts per 1,000 under UK Hallmarking Act 1973)
karat_purity_reference.ring_suitability_note: Slightly higher gold purity than exact fractional 14/24 (58.5% vs 58.33%); common on European-hallmarked rings.

karat_purity_reference.label: 14K Solid Gold (U.S. Fractional 14/24)
karat_purity_reference.legal_status_us_uk: Most common US engagement ring alloy; 15 U.S.C. § 295 allows max 0.003 unsoldered / 0.007 soldered tolerance.
karat_purity_reference.ring_suitability_note: Strongest balance of daily scratch/prong durability and substantial gold content (58.33% fine gold).

karat_purity_reference.label: 10K Solid Gold (U.S. Minimum Karat Gold)
karat_purity_reference.legal_status_us_uk: Minimum legal karat threshold to be called 'Karat Gold' in the United States without qualification (16 CFR § 23.3).
karat_purity_reference.ring_suitability_note: Contains 58.33% base alloy metals; harder and pale yellow, lower intrinsic gold value and higher potential skin sensitivity.

karat_purity_reference.label: 9K Gold (Below U.S. 10K Threshold)
karat_purity_reference.legal_status_us_uk: Legal minimum in UK (375 fineness under Hallmarking Act 1973), but CANNOT be marketed simply as 'Gold' in US without percentage disclosure (16 CFR § 23.3).
karat_purity_reference.ring_suitability_note: Buyer warning for US shoppers importing UK/Australian rings: contains only 37.5% pure gold.

regulatory_and_testing_standards.category: U.S. Federal Statute — Mandatory Maker's Mark
regulatory_and_testing_standards.title: National Gold and Silver Marking Act (15 U.S.C. Chapter 8, §§ 291–300)
regulatory_and_testing_standards.key_rule: Under 15 U.S.C. § 297(b), any article bearing a quality mark (such as 10K, 14K, 18K, 585, or 750) MUST also bear the registered U.S. trademark or legal name of the manufacturer/importer in lettering at least as large as and positioned as close as possible to the quality mark. Under 15 U.S.C. § 295, assay deviation cannot exceed 3 parts per 1,000 (unsoldered) or 7 parts per 1,000 (soldered).
regulatory_and_testing_standards.checklist_relevance: Directly backs Checklist Item #3: a standalone '14K' or '18K' stamp with NO maker's mark violates federal marking requirements and is a major counterfeit indicator.

regulatory_and_testing_standards.category: U.S. FTC Jewelry Guides — Solid Gold vs Plated / Vermeil / Filled
regulatory_and_testing_standards.title: FTC Guides for the Jewelry, Precious Metals, and Pewter Industries (16 CFR Part 23)
regulatory_and_testing_standards.key_rule: Under 16 CFR § 23.3 & § 23.4: Unqualified 'Karat Gold' must be composed throughout of at least 10K gold. 'Gold Plated' / 'Gold Electroplated' requires >= 0.175 microns (electrolytic) or >= 0.5 microns; 'Heavy Gold Electroplate' requires >= 2.5 microns; 'Vermeil' is sterling silver plated with >= 2.5 microns (100 millionths of an inch) of gold; 'Gold Filled' / 'Rolled Gold Plate' is mechanically bonded gold coating (typically 1/20th total weight) over base metal.
regulatory_and_testing_standards.checklist_relevance: Directly backs Checklist Items #1 & #2: reject listings described as plated, vermeil, gold-filled, gold overlay, rolled gold, PVD, or gold-tone.

regulatory_and_testing_standards.title: UK Hallmarking Act 1973 & Assay Office Guidance
regulatory_and_testing_standards.key_rule: Gold articles over 1.0 gram sold in the UK must carry an independent Assay Office hallmark comprising a sponsor's mark, millesimal fineness mark (375, 585, 750, 916, or 999), and Assay Office town mark (London leopard's head, Birmingham anchor, Sheffield rose, Edinburgh castle).
regulatory_and_testing_standards.checklist_relevance: Provides pre-sale third-party laboratory assay verification when buying from UK-hallmarked makers.

regulatory_and_testing_standards.title: GIA Gems & Gemology (Winter 2024): XRF Elemental Testing
regulatory_and_testing_standards.key_rule: Energy-dispersive X-ray fluorescence (EDXRF / XRF) accurately measures gold alloy composition non-destructively in seconds without scratching or acid damage, and typically detects base metals or nickel underlayers beneath thin plating.
regulatory_and_testing_standards.checklist_relevance: Directly backs Checklist Items #10 & #11: request professional XRF testing upon arrival before resizing or wearing.

regulatory_and_testing_standards.category: Counterfeit Deception Alert — Heavy Gold-Plated Low-Karat / Electroformed Cores
regulatory_and_testing_standards.title: GIA Carlsbad Lab Notes (Summer 2025 'Gold-Plated Gold' & Spring 2024 'Electroformed Gold')
regulatory_and_testing_standards.key_rule: GIA laboratories documented deceptive pieces in 2024–2025 where 10K gold coated with heavy pure gold plating read falsely as 14K or 18K on surface XRF, and electroformed wax/resin cores with ~200-micron gold shells passed surface XRF alone.
regulatory_and_testing_standards.checklist_relevance: Proves why buyers should ask the independent jeweler for BOTH XRF testing AND calibrated gram weight + specific gravity / microscopic seam inspection.

regulatory_and_testing_standards.title: GIA Bench Tip #9: Touchstone Nitric Acid & Aqua Regia Testing
regulatory_and_testing_standards.key_rule: Compares metal streak against calibrated 10K, 14K, 18K, and 22K test needles using nitric acid (<=14K) and aqua regia (18K+). Leaves a slight rub mark if taken directly on the shank—never allow scraping without consent before your return window closes.
regulatory_and_testing_standards.checklist_relevance: Explains why non-destructive XRF + specific gravity is strictly preferred while a ring is still inside its return window.
